newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey parliament considers Erbakan censure bid.
newsitem.headline: Turkey parliament considers Erbakan censure bid.

text.p: Turkey's parliament on Wednesday began debating a bid by the secularist opposition to topple the country's first Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan.
"Let the debate begin," Uluc Gurkan, deputy speaker of parliament, told the house.
Parliamentary sources said MPs were expected to vote later in the day on whether to proceed with a formal censure motion that would force the government to resign.
However, analysts said Erbakan and his conservative coalition partner Tansu Ciller were virtually certain to survive their first such test since taking power in late June.

Opposition MPS are angered by Erbakan's bid to redirect foreign policy towards Turkey's Arab and Moslem neighbours, a move that has drawn fire from the secular opposition, elements of the armed forces and Ankara's close patron Washington.
On paper the opposition needs 276 votes, a majority of the 550 seats, to guarantee victory.
It can count on up to 269 MPs from its own ranks, plus a handful of dissidents from Erbakan's coalition ally, the conservative True Path Party led by Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller.
Gencay Gurun, an MP from Ciller's party, handed in her resignation to parliament shortly before Wednesday's debate.
Gurun had voted against Ciller's alliance with the Islamists in the government's July vote of confidence and opposed Erbakan's recent trip to Libya.
The iron discipline of Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party all but bars defections.
